skills.name: Telecommunications: access and the digital divide

note.text: The digital divide concerns unequal ability to access and use digital communication. Coverage is one condition; affordability, reliable power, suitable devices, skills, language and accessibility also matter. Owning a phone does not prove that a person can use a needed online service. Differences can occur within a town, between rural and urban places or among age and income groups.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to compare barriers to meaningful digital access and propose a matched response. Builds on: signals and networks. Leads to: Cameroon access planning and trade information.

sections.heading: Explain the geography

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: In an invented village comparison, the network reaches both households. One cannot afford regular data; another has access but needs help using the service language. Coverage expansion alone does not solve either problem. ITU’s meaningful-connectivity approach considers capabilities and usable access, rather than treating signal coverage as complete inclusion.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Specify the barrier from the evidence. Match a response to affordability, skills, accessibility or reliability, and say what else remains. Do not infer ability, interest or income from residence alone.

a cost that prevents practical use
